name: frontend-template
_what_this_is: A minimal, dependency-free single-page frontend project that exists so a new frontend skill has a working starting point instead of re-deriving the same boilerplate. Copy the contents into the project, rename what needs renaming, and delete what the task does not need.
_why_it_exists: Step 2 of this skill's process: 'Writing a frontend webapp requires the same boilerplate HTML/CSS each time, so assets/frontend-template/ is the reusable artefact.' This file is that artefact's index.
_provenance: Authored from the description of assets/frontend-template/ in this skill's SKILL.md and references; no original copy was recovered. The structure, the three progressive-enhancement behaviours, and the token/base CSS split are a reconstruction chosen to satisfy that description, not a recovered file. Every value in tokens.css is a stand-in to be replaced.
_how_to_use: 1. Copy this directory's contents into the target project. 2. Open index.html and replace the title, the meta description, and the content in <main>. 3. Open styles/tokens.css and replace the :root block with the project's real tokens — do not style against the placeholders. 4. Open app.js and wire the interactions the task actually needs. 5. Delete anything unused. A template with unused files left in it is a template nobody has read.
_what_it_is_not: Not a framework, not a build step, not a component library. It is plain HTML, CSS, and one JavaScript file, so it runs from a file:// URL with nothing installed. That is the point: a template that needs npm install to evaluate is a template nobody evaluates.

_files.index.html: The page. Semantic landmarks, one h1, skip link, and the token stylesheet already linked.
_files.styles/tokens.css: Design tokens as CSS custom properties. The one file to edit to re-theme.
_files.styles/base.css: Reset, typography, and the handful of layout primitives.
_files.app.js: Progressive enhancement: a theme toggle, a nav disclosure, and a copy-to-clipboard button. Each is guarded, so removing one leaves the page working.

_conventions.tokens: Every colour, size, and duration comes from a custom property. A hard-coded hex in a rule is a defect in this template specifically.
_conventions.units: rem for type and space, so a browser zoom or a user font-size preference is honoured.
_conventions.accessibility: Landmarks, a skip link, visible focus rings that are not removed, and a reduced-motion block. Kept because a template that drops them teaches the wrong default.
_conventions.dark_mode: Both schemes declared, with light as the default. A dark-only template is a decision the template should not make for you.

_checks_before_shipping: Tab through the page: focus order follows reading order and every control is reachable.
Zoom to 200% and check nothing is clipped or overlapping.
Toggle the OS dark-mode setting and re-check contrast in both schemes.
Run with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce set. Nothing should move.
Search for a hard-coded colour outside styles/tokens.css. There should be none.
Delete the sample content. A template with lorem ipsum in it ships lorem ipsum.
